network.overall_strategy: Represent glutamate as non-stereospecific 2-aminopentanedioic acid. The network is organized around 2-oxoglutarate as the main convergence hub, with four literature-supported entries: hydrothermal Fe2+-mediated pyruvate plus glyoxylate aldol chemistry, surface pyruvate plus glyoxylate aldol chemistry, surface 3-oxalomalate decarboxylation to 4-hydroxy-2-oxoglutarate, and hydrothermal oxidation of 2-hydroxyglutarate. Ten pathways are obtained by combining these entries with two hydrothermal N-installation reactions and by adding an orthogonal surface dinitrile route that bypasses 2-oxoglutarate. H2, H2O, CO2, and NH3 are written explicitly so redox and hydrolysis steps are stoichiometrically closed and cross-link the branches.

reactions.name: Hydrothermal CO2/H2 fixation to pyruvate

conditions.other: anoxic, H2-rich serpentinization system; pyruvate is one product of multicarbon CO2 reduction

reactions.mechanism: Metal-surface CO2 reduction and C-C bond formation generate the C3 alpha-keto acid; the balanced net step is 3 CO2 + 5 H2 -> pyruvate + 3 H2O.
reactions.reasoning: Pyruvate is one of the multicarbon products observed in H2-driven CO2 reduction on hydrothermal Fe-bearing catalysts, as noted in the review's environmental context (Preiner et al., 2020). This is included as an upstream feedstock-extension step rather than a dedicated glutamate experiment, but it is chemically justified in serpentinization settings and connects the network back to simple inorganic carbon.

reactions.name: Fe2+-catalyzed pyruvate-glyoxylate aldol condensation

conditions.other: anoxic hydrothermal water; near-neutral to mildly alkaline vent-mixing conditions

reactions.mechanism: Fe2+-assisted aldol addition of the enolizable pyruvate C3 unit to the glyoxylate aldehyde forms the C5 hydroxyketo diacid.
reactions.reasoning: This C3 plus C2 carbon-carbon bond-forming step is directly supported in the iron-driven protometabolic network of Muchowska et al. (2019). Related pyruvate plus glyoxylate coupling also appears in the linked glyoxylate chemistry of Springsteen et al. (2018), reinforcing the prebiotic plausibility of this entry to the 2-oxoglutarate family.

reactions.name: Surface pyruvate-glyoxylate aldol condensation
reactions.mechanism: Non-enzymatic aldol coupling of pyruvate and glyoxylate in surface water furnishes the same C5 hydroxyketo diacid obtained in hydrothermal iron chemistry.
reactions.reasoning: Springsteen et al. (2018) showed that pyruvate and glyoxylate can furnish 4-hydroxy-2-oxoglutarate at ambient temperature within linked glyoxylate chemistry. This creates a surface entry to the glutamate network, although coupling this ambient step to the hotter downstream iron-mediated chemistry remains an open systems-level question.

reactions.name: 3-oxalomalate decarboxylation to 4-hydroxy-2-oxoglutarate

conditions.other: ambient surface water; decarboxylation on hour timescales

reactions.mechanism: Oxidative decarboxylation of the oxalyl-bearing C6 tricarboxylate liberates CO2 and yields the C5 hydroxyketo diacid.
reactions.reasoning: Springsteen et al. (2018) demonstrated decarboxylation of 3-oxalomalate to 4-hydroxy-2-oxoglutarate at about 296 K on hour timescales. It is therefore a credible surface source of the immediate C5 precursor feeding the downstream hydrothermal branch.

reactions.name: Dehydration of 4-hydroxy-2-oxoglutarate

conditions.other: anoxic hydrothermal fluid; can act on surface-delivered mol_008 after transport

reactions.mechanism: Fe2+-assisted beta-elimination removes water from the C4 hydroxy group to generate the conjugated unsaturated dicarbonyl.
reactions.reasoning: Muchowska et al. (2019) reported Fe2+-promoted dehydration of 4-hydroxy-2-oxoglutarate to the unsaturated C5 dicarbonyl. This step is directly supported under hydrothermal iron chemistry; when mol_008 originates at the surface, the required transfer into a hotter iron-rich setting remains a plausible but not yet one-pot-demonstrated systems connection (Muchowska et al., 2019; Springsteen et al., 2018).

reactions.name: Reduction of 4-oxopent-2-enedioate to 2-oxoglutarate

conditions.other: mildly reducing hydrothermal water with dissolved H2

reactions.mechanism: Reduction of the C=C bond saturates the unsaturated C5 intermediate and yields the alpha-keto diacid 2-oxoglutarate.
reactions.reasoning: Muchowska et al. (2019) observed iron-promoted reduction of the unsaturated intermediate to 2-oxoglutarate. H2 is written explicitly as the net reductant so the step is stoichiometrically closed; experimentally the reducing power is likely mediated by Fe chemistry and hydrothermal redox gradients rather than free homogeneous H2 alone.

reactions.name: Hydrothermal oxidation of 2-hydroxyglutarate

conditions.other: anoxic hydrothermal fluid; pH and redox state control equilibrium

reactions.mechanism: Dehydrogenation of the alpha-hydroxy acid to the corresponding alpha-keto acid releases H2.
reactions.reasoning: Lee et al. (2014) identified 2-hydroxyglutarate to 2-oxoglutarate conversion in hydrothermal fluids and specifically reported oxidation to the keto acid with H2 release. This makes 2-hydroxyglutarate a short entry to the hub molecule, while also highlighting that prolonged hydrothermal exposure can compete with alpha-keto-acid preservation.

reactions.name: Iron-promoted reductive amination of 2-oxoglutarate with hydroxylamine

conditions.other: anoxic water; hydroxylamine available; H2 written as net reducing equivalent

reactions.mechanism: Condensation of the alpha-keto group with hydroxylamine gives an oxime/imino intermediate that is reduced on iron to the alpha-amino acid.
reactions.reasoning: Muchowska et al. (2019) demonstrated iron-promoted conversion of 2-oxoglutarate to glutamate using hydroxylamine as the nitrogen donor. The graph writes H2 explicitly as the net reducing equivalent so the reaction is redox-balanced; experimentally the reducing power is supplied by Fe0/Fe2+ under hydrothermal conditions. Hydroxylamine availability remains a prebiotic uncertainty, so this route is experimentally supported but geochemically less secure than direct NH3 amination. The product is shown as non-stereospecific glutamate because homochirality is unresolved.

reactions.name: FeS-catalyzed reductive amination of 2-oxoglutarate with ammonia

conditions.other: alkaline vent-like, H2-rich conditions; pH 9-11 plausible

reactions.mechanism: Ammonia forms an imine with the alpha-keto group and FeS facilitates surface-bound reduction to the alpha-amino acid.
reactions.reasoning: Kitadai et al. (2019) showed FeS promotes reductive amination of 2-oxoglutarate with ammonia in alkaline hydrothermal systems. H2 is written explicitly as the net reductant, consistent with H2-rich serpentinization settings; the study establishes the FeS-surface chemistry even though direct efficiency comparisons with the Fe0/Fe2+/hydroxylamine system remain open.

reactions.name: Amination of 2-hydroxypentanedinitrile

conditions.other: cyanosulfidic evaporitic pool; NH3-rich; upstream UV chemistry generates the hydroxydinitrile

reactions.mechanism: Amination of the cyanohydrin-derived center converts the hydroxydinitrile to the aminodinitrile with net water elimination.
reactions.reasoning: Patel et al. (2015) reported this NH3-driven conversion within the cyanosulfidic framework. Writing H2O as coproduct closes the net stoichiometry for the amination of the hydroxydinitrile and makes the surface nitrile branch chemically explicit.

reactions.name: Hydrolysis of 2-aminopentanedinitrile to glutamate

conditions.other: surface aqueous hydrolysis aided by concentration and pH cycling

reactions.mechanism: Sequential hydration of both nitriles to amides and then carboxylic acids converts the aminodinitrile into the dicarboxylic amino acid.
reactions.reasoning: Patel et al. (2015) showed that aminodinitrile hydrolysis yields glutamate. The balanced net transformation requires four waters and releases two equivalents of ammonia; writing NH3 explicitly this way corrects the common under-specified prose shorthand. The long-term stability of the C5 dinitriles under fluctuating UV, pH, and drying remains an open issue noted for cyanosulfidic surface chemistry.

pathways.name: Hydrothermal Fe2+ aldol route with FeS finish
pathways.description: Pyruvate and glyoxylate couple under hydrothermal Fe2+, then dehydrate and reduce to 2-oxoglutarate, which is aminated with NH3 on FeS.

pathways.name: Hydrothermal Fe2+ aldol route with hydroxylamine finish
pathways.description: The same hydrothermal carbon-skeleton-building sequence ends with Fe0/Fe2+-mediated reductive amination using hydroxylamine.

pathways.name: Surface aldol entry with FeS finish
pathways.description: Surface pyruvate plus glyoxylate aldol chemistry generates 4-hydroxy-2-oxoglutarate, then a hydrothermal handoff enables dehydration, reduction, and FeS/NH3 amination.

pathways.name: Surface aldol entry with hydroxylamine finish
pathways.description: A surface aldol step furnishes 4-hydroxy-2-oxoglutarate, which then enters hydrothermal dehydration and reduction before Fe0/Fe2+-driven hydroxylamine amination.

pathways.name: Oxalomalate entry with FeS finish
pathways.description: 3-Oxalomalate decarboxylates at the surface to 4-hydroxy-2-oxoglutarate, which then enters the hydrothermal dehydration, reduction, and FeS amination sequence.

pathways.name: Oxalomalate entry with hydroxylamine finish
pathways.description: Surface oxalomalate decarboxylation supplies 4-hydroxy-2-oxoglutarate, followed by hydrothermal dehydration, reduction, and Fe0/Fe2+-assisted hydroxylamine amination.

pathways.name: 2-Hydroxyglutarate oxidation with FeS finish
pathways.description: Hydrothermal oxidation of 2-hydroxyglutarate gives 2-oxoglutarate and H2, followed by FeS-catalyzed ammonia incorporation.

pathways.name: 2-Hydroxyglutarate oxidation with hydroxylamine finish
pathways.description: 2-Hydroxyglutarate is oxidized to the keto-acid hub, then Fe0/Fe2+ and hydroxylamine deliver glutamate; additional H2 can be supplied by the vent fluid.

pathways.name: Cyanosulfidic dinitrile route
pathways.description: A surface nitrile pathway converts 2-hydroxypentanedinitrile to the aminodinitrile and hydrolyzes both nitriles to the dicarboxylic amino acid, bypassing 2-oxoglutarate.

pathways.name: CO2-fed pyruvate extension of the hydrothermal route
pathways.description: Hydrothermal CO2/H2 fixation first supplies pyruvate; pyruvate then couples with glyoxylate and proceeds through dehydration, reduction, and FeS-catalyzed amination to glutamate.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Strong hydrothermal route. The Fe2+-promoted aldol, dehydration, and reduction steps are well supported, and the FeS amination finish is chemically credible. Slightly lower than P2 because the upstream iron sequence and the final FeS amination are drawn from different experimental systems, and H2 is treated as an assumed environmental reductant.
suggestions: Mark H2 as an environmental input or explicitly couple this pathway to an H2-producing branch.
Clarify how the Fe2+-driven upstream sequence transitions into the FeS-catalyzed amination step within one hydrothermal setting.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: This is the best-supported pathway by direct literature alignment: it matches the Muchowska hydrothermal iron sequence from pyruvate plus glyoxylate to glutamate. The main correction is rxn_008, which should be written as 2-oxoglutarate + hydroxylamine + 2 H2 -> glutamate + 2 H2O; hydroxylamine availability remains a known caveat from the literature.
suggestions: Correct rxn_008 stoichiometry to include 2 H2 and 2 H2O.
Mark H2 as an environmental input or explicitly couple the pathway to an H2-producing branch.
Note the known uncertainty in prebiotic hydroxylamine supply.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: The surface aldol entry is supported, and the downstream hydrothermal chemistry is sound. Confidence is limited mainly by the unmodeled transfer of 4-hydroxy-2-oxoglutarate from a surface setting into a hydrothermal Fe-driven sequence.
suggestions: Add an explicit transport or concentration step for 4-hydroxy-2-oxoglutarate between environments.
Specify ambient surface conditions for rxn_003 and hydrothermal Fe2+/FeS conditions for downstream steps.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Chemically plausible mixed-environment route, but weaker than P3 because the final hydroxylamine amination has the same stoichiometric correction and prebiotic availability caveat as P2. Surface-to-hydrothermal transfer is also only implicit.
suggestions: Correct rxn_008 to require 2 H2 and produce 2 H2O.
Add a transport justification for moving 4-hydroxy-2-oxoglutarate from surface to hydrothermal settings.
State Fe0/Fe2+ conditions for the amination step.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: A strong route: 3-oxalomalate decarboxylation is well aligned with Springsteen, and the hydrothermal conversion of the C5 intermediate to glutamate is chemically reasonable. As with P3, the main gap is explicit justification for moving the C5 intermediate between environments.
suggestions: Add an explicit transport or preservation step for 4-hydroxy-2-oxoglutarate between surface and hydrothermal settings.
Annotate ambient surface conditions for rxn_004 and hydrothermal Fe2+/FeS conditions for the downstream steps.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: The oxalomalate entry is well supported, but the hydroxylamine finish reduces confidence relative to P5. rxn_008 needs corrected coefficients, and the surface-to-hydrothermal handoff remains implicit rather than modeled.
suggestions: Correct rxn_008 to 2-oxoglutarate + hydroxylamine + 2 H2 -> glutamate + 2 H2O.
Add an explicit transfer step or transport rationale for the C5 intermediate.
Note the hydroxylamine availability caveat.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Compact and attractive hydrothermal pathway. rxn_007 and rxn_009 are both literature-supported, and the H2 produced in rxn_007 can directly supply the H2 consumed in rxn_009, giving good redox closure. The main uncertainty is whether 2-hydroxyglutarate oxidation is sufficiently productive relative to competing hydrothermal decomposition.
suggestions: State the hydrothermal pH/redox window for rxn_007 to show favorable oxidation to 2-oxoglutarate.
Annotate FeS explicitly for rxn_009 and note expected NH3 availability.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Short route, but weaker than P7. After correcting rxn_008 to require 2 H2, the H2 produced by a single rxn_007 event is insufficient, so the stated 2-step pathway is not internally redox-closed without additional reducing power. Hydroxylamine availability is also a known challenge.
suggestions: Correct rxn_008 stoichiometry to include 2 H2 and 2 H2O.
Add an external H2 source or couple two oxidations to one amination if internal redox closure is intended.
State Fe0/Fe2+ conditions and note the hydroxylamine caveat.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: The cyanosulfidic dinitrile bypass is literature-backed and reaches glutamate cleanly without using 2-oxoglutarate. The main correction is rxn_011: per the deterministic balance check it should be 2-aminopentanedinitrile + 4 H2O -> glutamate + 2 NH3. Hydrolysis conditions are also more demanding than the generic surface label suggests.
suggestions: Correct rxn_011 stoichiometry to consume 4 H2O and release 2 NH3.
Clarify whether the dinitrile hydrolysis is neutral, acidic, basic, or driven by wet-dry cycling.
Add more detail on the experimental context for rxn_010, which is mechanistically simplified as direct amination.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Assuming this pathway is rxn_001 -> rxn_002 -> rxn_005 -> rxn_006 -> rxn_009, it is coherent and hydrothermal throughout. Confidence is limited by rxn_001, which is a coarse net fixation step that needs explicit coefficients and mineral catalysis, and by the pathway label not naming its terminal amination step explicitly.
suggestions: Write rxn_001 explicitly as 3 CO2 + 5 H2 -> pyruvate + 3 H2O and name the mineral catalyst system.
State explicitly whether the terminal amination is rxn_009 or rxn_008.
If H2 is intended as an environmental input for this route, mark it as such in the node metadata.

evaluation.network_feedback: Connected, literature-aligned network with 15 molecules and 11 reactions; no isolated subgraphs and no reactions are UNBALANCED by the deterministic check, so there are no hard conservation failures. P2 is the best-supported single pathway by direct match to the Muchowska hydrothermal iron sequence, while P7 is a strong redox-coherent alternative. The main hydrothermal 2-oxoglutarate-centered branches and the dinitrile bypass all plausibly reach glutamate. The main fixes are specification issues: rxn_001 should be written explicitly as 3 CO2 + 5 H2 -> pyruvate + 3 H2O and given a mineral catalyst; rxn_008 should be 2-oxoglutarate + hydroxylamine + 2 H2 -> glutamate + 2 H2O; rxn_011 should be 2-aminopentanedinitrile + 4 H2O -> glutamate + 2 NH3 per the balance check. Cross-environment transfer in P3-P6 is plausible but only qualitatively justified, H2 and NH3 are better tagged as environmental inputs unless internal coupling is intended, the dinitrile hydrolysis conditions are underspecified, and P10 should explicitly name its terminal amination step. Overall this is an excellent network, closely aligned with Muchowska, Springsteen, Kitadai, Lee, and Patel et al., though per-reaction citations and explicit caveat annotations would improve confidence further.
